columns.fragility_note: Annual ecosystem output proxy (Pelt dataset). Raw values spanned negatives and values > 1; per-column min-max normalization applied.
columns.manipulability_note: Annual aggregation may mask intra-year seasonal dynamics.

columns.fragility_note: Resilience proxy (Pelt dataset). Raw values outside [0,1]; min-max normalized.
columns.manipulability_note: Resilience interpretation depends on population model assumptions underlying Pelt dataset.

columns.fragility_note: Integration/interaction proxy (Pelt dataset). Raw values outside [0,1]; min-max normalized.
columns.manipulability_note: Species interaction strength estimates are model-dependent.

columns.fragility_note: Resource demand proxy (Pelt dataset). Raw values outside [0,1]; min-max normalized.
columns.manipulability_note: Demand proxy derived from harvested pelt counts; susceptible to market price fluctuations.

columns.fragility_note: Stability proxy (Pelt dataset). Was already in [0,1] range in raw data.
columns.manipulability_note: Pelt harvest records from Hudson Bay Company may underrepresent true population levels.

notes: Pelt ecology pilot dataset derived from the classic Hudson Bay Company lynx-hare pelt records (Pelt dataset), covering annual observations from 1845 to 1935 (91 rows). O=ecosystem output proxy, R=resilience proxy, I=integration/interaction proxy, demand=resource demand proxy, S=stability proxy. All ORIC columns were outside [0,1] in raw form (negatives and values > 1) and have been normalized per-column using min-max scaling. This is a canonical ecological time series illustrating predator-prey dynamics and population cycles.
